findings.title: Per-share valuation ignores the customer penny warrants (up to 320M shares, about 19% of diluted shares) and the related contra-revenue
findings.detail: The 10-Q (periodic.txt, Note 14, line ~1425) says AMD issued warrants to two customers (Oct 2025, Feb 2026), 'each entitling the holder the right to purchase up to 160 million shares of the Company's common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per share'. The risk factor (line ~2368) puts the combined total at up to 320 million shares. Line ~1439 says the weighted-average fair value is $178.58 per share 'as most market conditions had been met'. Line ~1441 reports a warrant liability of $1.2 billion and $4.5 billion of unrecognized grant-date fair value 'that would be recorded as a reduction of revenue'. valuation.json divides equity value by diluted_shares = 1,661M, which excludes all warrant shares (none have vested). share_change_qoq (+0.2%/qtr) is based only on the historical diluted-share trend. Neither valuation_inputs.json nor assumptions.json nor note.md mentions the warrants as potential dilution. Yet the DCF capitalises the Data Center/Helios ramp (Q-3, Q-4), and the purchase milestones that vest these warrants are tied to that same ramp. So the model takes the revenue but not the dilution attached to it. Illustrative full-dilution effect (my arithmetic from valuation.json, not a code output): DCF equity $324.5bn / 1,981M shares = about $164 versus $195.37; relative leg $748.0bn / 1,981M = about $378 versus $450.35; blended about $249 versus $297, a cut of roughly 16% in the target price. Under the policy bands the rating stays Underperform (upside about -48% instead of -38.6%), but a possible 16% swing in the target, undisclosed, is a material valuation omission. Separately, the $4.5bn of unrecognized warrant value will reduce reported revenue as qualifying revenue is recognised. Guidance probably already nets this out for FY2026Q4, but the rationale for later-year revenue/FCF does not mention it. The $1.2bn warrant liability (other long-term liabilities) is reasonably left out of net cash because it is equity-settled at $0.01, but that choice should be stated.
evidence: snapshot/docs/periodic.txt (Note 14 customer warrants: 160M shares each at $0.01; $178.58/share fair value; $1.2bn liability; $4.5bn unrecognized grant-date fair value)
snapshot/docs/periodic.txt (risk factor: warrants exercisable for up to a combined 320 million shares)
findings.required_evidence: valuation_inputs.json rationales (and a sentence in note.md's valuation section or risks) acknowledge the customer warrants (up to 320M shares at $0.01, quotable from periodic.txt) as potential dilution not reflected in the code's diluted share count. They state the direction and rough size of the effect on the per-share target (and confirm the rating would not change), or explain with evidence why the dilution is treated as immaterial or not probable. They also note that the unrecognized warrant value will reduce future reported revenue, and state why the warrant liability is excluded from net cash.

findings.title: Data-source disclosure still does not name the earnings-release accession (price provider now named)
findings.detail: Partly repaired. The Disclosures line now names the price provider ('unadjusted daily close from the Yahoo Finance chart endpoint (split-adjusted by the provider)', which matches the snapshot/prices.json note) and says peer market values come from the same feed. It also identifies the release as the Form 8-K exhibit EX-99.1, 'a separate EDGAR accession', and as the source of the guidance and demand quotes. The literal release accession 0000002488-26-000188 (snapshot/manifest.json, docs/release_ex99_1.txt) is still not named. gen-writer reports that the untagged_number gate would flag the digits and that values.json has no key for this accession. I checked values.json and confirmed it has no such key, only trigger_accession. Policy section 6 is satisfied because the trigger accession, cutoff and price date are present. The as-of trail is still incomplete by one identifier. Closing this needs a compute-side values key (for example release_accession) that the writer can reference as {{key}}.

resolved.evidence: generator/note.md Results net-income bullet (rendered in numerical/recompute/note_rendered.md) now cites both one-off items by verbatim quote: [[Q-7]] (discrete tax benefit related to stock-based compensation of $772 million, periodic.txt lines 1481/1732) and [[Q-11]] (noncash charge of $1.2 billion from warrant-liability remeasurement within Other income (expense), net, periodic.txt line 1441). The claim that 'reported EPS overstates the recurring earnings run rate' has been removed. It is replaced by a labelled judgment that the two items move EPS in opposite directions and that their net effect cannot be determined from the filing. That judgment is consistent with the evidence: the 10-Q gives no after-tax effect for the warrant charge (the income-tax note at line 1481 and the warrant note at lines 1425-1441 give none). The amounts appear only inside verbatim quotes, and all quotes Q-1 to Q-11 match snapshot/docs text exactly.

valuation_inputs.json rationales.peers now has a TTM period-alignment paragraph. It gives AMD's TTM end of 2026-09-26 and each peer's: INTC 2026-09-26 (aligned), NVDA 2026-07-26, AVGO 2026-08-02, MRVL 2026-08-01. It says the lag biases EV/Sales and the median upward, because NVDA and MRVL, both lagged, are the two middle values (median 16.27x = mean of MRVL 16.07x and NVDA 16.48x in numerical/recompute/peers.json). It says the multiple is not adjusted and that the relative leg should be read as generous. I checked the dates and the cited growth against snapshot/peers.json filtered to acceptance at or before the cutoff: NVDA quarterly Revenues $81.615bn (to 2026-04-26) then $96.221bn (to 2026-07-26); MRVL $2.4178bn then $2.7393bn; latest ends NVDA 2026-07-26, AVGO 2026-08-02, MRVL 2026-08-01, INTC 2026-09-26. All match.

note_rendered.md: the Results heading no longer tags the section '(SEC XBRL data)'. It now reads 'the financial figures are derived by code from SEC XBRL data, and quoted text is taken from the 10-Q'. The final disclosure reads 'All figures are generated by code and are unaudited by the author. Reported financial figures are derived from SEC XBRL data. Guidance figures ($17.0bn revenue, 55.0% non-GAAP gross margin) are taken from the quoted earnings-release text, not XBRL. The share price and peer market values come from the price feed named above.' This separates XBRL-derived figures, release-quoted guidance and price-feed data, and the policy section 6 code/unaudited statement is still present.
